policy: Coverage gaps, not raw catalogue growth, determine research order: lowest cell count, then lowest neighborhood count, then scarcest citywide category; stable Bulgarian alphabetical ties.
One approved business ID counts once per actual service category in one sourced neighborhood. Multiple services or staff do not create extra businesses.
A real multiservice premises can legitimately occupy several categories; business-category incidence totals are not unique-business totals.
An exact parent label never fills its numbered children; additional named areas and ambiguous broad labels remain distinct.
Mobile/service-area providers are reported separately, never multiplied across neighborhoods. Expired, future, draft, rejected and owner-excluded records cannot fill cells.
Priority cells marked service_area_evidence call for documented coverage-area review, not invented physical offices or automatic citywide fanout.
A target is not proof that 30 eligible premises exist in every cell. Genuine shortages remain open; never invent businesses, tariffs, coordinates or duplicate branches.

Located counts mean currently usable exact-address bindings, including legacy first-party pairs; they are not independent geographic or entrance verification, a completed radius-coverage test or guaranteed availability.
This maintenance report changes no filtering, ranking, category mappings, registration, booking, database or production configuration.
